areas.name: Savage River State Forest
areas.manager: Maryland Department of Natural Resources, Maryland Forest Service
areas.note: In its State Wildlands you may hunt, fish and trap only if otherwise permitted; motor vehicles, wheeled transport such as game carts, and temporary structures and equipment are barred. Ask about portable stands.
areas.waterNote: Rules from COMAR 08.02.11.01 and the 2026 Maryland fishing guide. Savage River mainstem and tributaries above the reservoir dam: artificial flies and lures only, no bait or scented devices, no brook trout kept; the guide adds 2 other trout daily, 4 in possession, and bars barbed hooks, which the regulation doesn't, so use barbless. That area excludes Savage River Reservoir, New Germany Lake and the river from the reservoir up to Poplar Lick Run. The stretch up to Poplar Lick is closed to all fishing from the first Sunday after March 4 to the last Saturday in March, apart from a youth day for under-16s; no brook trout kept, and usual fishing hours are 5:30 a.m. to 10 p.m. Dam down to the Allegany Bridge: artificial flies only on conventional fly tackle, no centerpin, spinning, spincast or casting reels. Allegany Bridge down to the Route 135 bridge: artificial lures or flies with a single hook, no treble hooks. Both stretches below the dam: open all year, no bait or scented devices, 2 trout daily, 4 in possession, brook trout 12 inches and brown trout 18 inches minimum. Ask DNR Fisheries at 301-334-8218.

hunting.summary: Allowed in season with a Maryland license, except posted safety zones, Big Run and New Germany State Parks, and private land without written permission; Savage Highlands and Savage River Reservoir have their own entries. No baiting, stands must cause no tree damage and be removed daily, and Sunday hunting is limited; call headquarters, 301-895-5759.
hunting.quote: Hunting is permitted throughout Savage River State Forest except where posted with safety zone signs.

trapping.summary: Allowed on land and in water with a written permit, a hunting license and DNR trapper education certificate, but the permit isn't shown to cover the state parks inside the forest or Savage River Reservoir. The hunting guide lists 301-895-5759 for permits; the forest page says DNR's Flintstone office issues them, so call first.
trapping.quote: Trapping is permitted on land and in water throughout the forest. Permits are issued at the Regional DNR Wildlife Office in Flintstone.

fishing.summary: Finfish only with a Maryland license, outside posted areas; much of the Savage River is limited to flies or lures, with special trout limits, and the stretch from the reservoir up to Poplar Lick closes for most of March. See the water rules and ask DNR Fisheries at 301-334-8218 first.
fishing.quote: A person may use only artificial flies and lures

gathering.summary: Maryland DNR's stated position is that state forest and park rules bar removing plants and natural items, so don't forage here. The rule doesn't name mushrooms, berries or nuts; call headquarters at 301-895-5759 with questions.
gathering.quote: Current Forest and Parks regulations prohibit removing or disturbing plants and natural items on State-owned public lands

ginseng.summary: Ginseng harvest isn't allowed here, even with a state collecting permit, because this is state land managed by Maryland DNR. Call headquarters at 301-895-5759 with questions.
ginseng.quote: As of the 2013 collecting season, ginseng harvest on state lands managed by the Maryland Department of Natural Resources is no longer permitted.

ramps.summary: The state forest rule bars removing or disturbing any plant without a permit, and we found no sign a permit is offered for ramps. The rule doesn't name ramps; call headquarters at 301-895-5759 with questions.
ramps.quote: Except as authorized in Regulation .03 of this chapter and §§C and D of this regulation, an individual may not remove, disturb, damage, or destroy any plant, rock, mineral, or animal in a State forest.

areas.name: Potomac-Garrett State Forest
areas.manager: Maryland Forest Service, Maryland Department of Natural Resources
areas.contact: Forest headquarters, 1431 Potomac Camp Road, Oakland, MD 21550; 301-707-6539; office hours listed as Monday, 7 am to 3:30 pm (staff often in the field, call ahead). Closed for unsafe bridges: Lostland Run Road at Campsite 22 and the 5½ Mile Trail bridge over Toliver Run; call for current closures.
areas.note: In its State Wildlands you may hunt, fish and trap only if otherwise permitted; motor vehicles, wheeled transport such as game carts, and temporary structures and equipment are barred. Ask about portable stands.
areas.waterNote: North Branch Potomac River, from the forest's lower boundary near Lostland Run up to its upper boundary at Wallman, is a delayed-harvest trout area under COMAR 08.02.11.01. From Oct 1 to June 15: no trout kept, no natural or live bait or scented lures, and no barbed hooks. From June 16 to Sept 30: five trout a day. Western Maryland Fisheries: 301-334-8218.

hunting.summary: Allowed in regular seasons except where posted with safety zone signs, with limited Sunday hunting; no baiting, and stands must come out with you each day. Herrington Manor and Swallow Falls State Parks are closed to hunting, and private land needs the owner's written permission; call 301-707-6539.
hunting.quote: Hunting is permitted throughout Potomac-Garrett State Forest except where posted with safety zone signs.

trapping.summary: Allowed on land and in water with a trapping permit from the DNR Wildlife Office at Mount Nebo WMA in Oakland, 301-334-4255. Apply with a valid hunting license, a letter from forest headquarters (301-707-6539) and a trapper education certificate.
trapping.quote: A trapping permit must be obtained from the Regional DNR Wildlife Office at Mount Nebo Wildlife Management Area in Oakland.

fishing.summary: On the North Branch from Oct 1 to June 15: keep no trout and use no bait or barbed hooks. Finfish are open outside posted areas with a Maryland freshwater license, plus a trout stamp for trout. Fishing for anything else needs a permit, and we found no sign one is offered here; ask 301-707-6539.
fishing.quote: Except in a posted area, an individual may fish in the waters of a State forest for finfish, if the individual complies with the State fishing laws.

areas.name: Green Ridge State Forest
areas.manager: Maryland Department of Natural Resources, Maryland Forest Service
areas.note: In its State Wildlands (Deep Run, Maple Run, Potomac Bends, Hoop Pole Hollow) you may hunt, fish and trap only if otherwise permitted; motor vehicles, wheeled transport such as game carts, and temporary structures and equipment are barred. Ask about portable stands and flood-closed roads.
areas.waterNote: Town Creek (two posted sections in the forest): from Oct. 1, catch and release only, with no natural or live bait, scented devices or barbed hooks. COMAR 08.02.11.01 ends this May 31, but DNR's Town Creek page says June 15, so follow June 15. Fifteen Mile Creek watershed: closed to all fishing from the first Sunday after March 4 through the last Saturday in March, per COMAR 08.02.11.01 (March 8-28 in 2026). Sideling Hill Creek: the forest recreation page lists stream closures, but the 2026 state fishing guide shows none, so ask DNR Fisheries at 301-334-8218.

hunting.summary: Allowed in regular seasons with a Maryland hunting license, except where safety zone signs are posted. No baiting, only stands you carry out each day, limited Sunday hunting and written landowner permission for private land in or next to the forest; call 301-478-3124.
hunting.quote: Hunting is permitted throughout Green Ridge State Forest except where posted with safety zone signs.

trapping.summary: Allowed on land and in water with a free forest trapping permit, a Maryland hunting license and a DNR trapper education certificate. The forest page says permits come from the DNR Wildlife Office in Flintstone and the state guide lists 301-478-3124, so call that number first.
trapping.quote: Trapping is permitted on land and in water throughout the forest. Permits are issued at the Regional DNR Wildlife Office in Flintstone.

fishing.summary: Town Creek's posted sections are catch and release from Oct 1, with no bait or barbed hooks. Finfish only, outside posted areas, with a Maryland license and, for trout, a stamp; we found no sign the permit for anything else is offered, so ask 301-478-3124. Fifteen Mile Creek watershed closes most of March and the forest page lists Sideling Hill Creek closures the guide doesn't show, so call DNR Fisheries at 301-334-8218.
fishing.quote: A valid Maryland Freshwater Fishing License is required.

ginseng.quote: As of the 2013 collecting season, ginseng harvest on state lands managed by the Maryland Department of Natural Resources is no longer permitted.

areas.name: Big Run State Park
areas.manager: Maryland Park Service, Maryland Department of Natural Resources (run from New Germany State Park)
areas.note: Big Run is a small park inside Savage River State Forest, and the rules change at the park boundary; from May 2027, Big Run Road will close just north of Savage River Road for up to four months.
areas.waterNote: Savage River and tributaries above the reservoir dam, apparently including Big Run and Monroe Run, except the put-and-take water below: artificial flies and lures only, no natural or live bait or scented devices, no brook trout in possession (COMAR 08.02.11.01 H(2)). Maryland's 2026 fishing guide also bars barbed hooks here, which the regulation does not list, and limits other trout to 2 a day and 4 in possession. Savage River from the reservoir up to Poplar Lick: put-and-take water, closed to all fishing from the first Sunday after March 4 to the last Saturday in March, except under-16 anglers on Youth Trout Fishing Day; brook trout can't be kept, other trout 5 a day and 10 in possession (COMAR 08.02.11.01 B and I). Savage River Reservoir, at the park's southern edge: COMAR 08.02.11.01 lists no closure and the same put-and-take limits, but DNR's reservoir page says "There is a brief lake closure each spring when trout stocking begins." Everywhere: nontidal license, plus a trout stamp at 16 and older to catch, try to catch or keep trout, per the state fishing guide.

hunting.summary: No hunting in the park. Hunting is permitted in the adjacent state forest, so know which side of the boundary you are on, and call (301) 895-5453 with questions.

trapping.summary: Not without a written permit, and we found no sign one is offered here. Ask the manager at (301) 895-5453.

areas.manager: Maryland Park Service, Maryland Department of Natural Resources

areas.waterNote: Casselman River from the two red posts on the south side of the I-68 eastbound bridge down to the Pennsylvania line is delayed-harvest trout water. From Oct. 1 through June 15, release all trout, don't carry or use natural or live bait or scented devices, and don't fish barbed hooks; from June 16 through Sept. 30, the limit is five trout daily and ten in possession (COMAR 08.02.11.01).

areas.name: Deep Creek Lake State Park
areas.manager: Maryland Park Service (Maryland Department of Natural Resources)
areas.note: The park is separate from the Deep Creek Lake Natural Resources Management Area, which handles the lake and its shoreline Buffer Strip, and the rules differ.
areas.waterNote: Deep Creek Lake: walleye have a 15-inch minimum, all fish 18 to 21 inches must be released, and the season is closed March 1 through April 15 (COMAR 08.02.11.04). The lake is put-and-take trout water with no closure: no brook trout kept, other trout 5 a day and 10 in possession (COMAR 08.02.11.01 B).

hunting.summary: Only inside the posted 551-acre area, Monday through Saturday, with weapons unloaded until inside it, no firearms hunting until October 15, no bait, and temporary stands and blinds removed daily. Waterfowl hunting is only at designated lake sites by permit and reservation, and other hunting is banned on the lake's Buffer Strip; call 301-387-5563.
hunting.quote: General hunting permitted in 551-acre designated hunting area

trapping.summary: Not without a written permit from the Superintendent of the Maryland Park Service, and we found no sign one is offered here, so ask the park at 301-387-5563. The hunting guide's trapping permit number, 301-334-4255, is for the separate Deep Creek Lake Natural Resources Management Area, not the park.
trapping.quote: Except by written permit, an individual may not trap or attempt to trap game in a State park.

fishing.summary: Allowed from shore and park docks with a Maryland license, plus a trout stamp at 16 and older to catch, try to catch or keep trout; release all brook trout and 18-to-21-inch walleye. No ranger docks, swim area or private docks; walleye season closed March 1 through April 15; non-finfish need a permit; call 301-387-5563.
fishing.quote: Anglers can fish from the shore and from the docks along the park shoreline.

areas.name: Herrington Manor State Park
areas.manager: Maryland Park Service (DNR)
areas.contact: Herrington Manor State Park, 222 Herrington Lane, Oakland, MD 21550, 301-334-9180
areas.note: The park sits within Potomac-Garrett State Forest, and many of its trails cross onto forest land that is open to hunting, so wear bright colors in season and know which land you are on.
areas.waterNote: Herrington Lake and the main stem of Herrington Creek are listed as put-and-take trout waters with no seasonal closure: release all brook trout and keep up to 5 other trout a day, 10 in possession. areas.name: New Germany State Park
areas.manager: Maryland Park Service (DNR)
areas.note: The park sits inside Savage River State Forest, but hunting is banned in the park and the forest's trapping permit doesn't replace the written permit park rules require. Cabins, campsites and pavilions will close at various times during water and wastewater work in 2026-2027.

hunting.summary: No hunting in the park, though the surrounding Savage River State Forest is open to it. In season, licensed hunters may carry across the park only to reach land open to hunting, firearms unloaded and cased or with breech open or broken, arrows in a quiver or case; call 301-895-5453.
hunting.quote: Big Run State Park and New Germany State Park are situated within the forest boundaries; hunting is prohibited in both state parks.

trapping.summary: Not without a written permit from the Superintendent of the Maryland Park Service, and we found no sign one is offered here. The forest's trapping permit comes from a different office and does not replace it, so ask the park at 301-895-5453.

areas.manager: Maryland Park Service, Maryland Department of Natural Resources (managed by the Deep Creek Lake State Park Complex)
areas.note: Park hours are 8 a.m. to sunset, and the park asks you to check first if any activity means being there before or after those hours; it names only fishing and boat launching as examples allowed outside them.
areas.waterNote: Youghiogheny River, from a red post about 100 yards above the Deep Creek Lake tailrace down 4 miles to the Sang Run Bridge: artificial lures only, no bait or scented devices, no barbed hooks, all trout released, under COMAR 08.02.11.01 C(3).

hunting.summary: Hunting is allowed only in the signed 122-acre area, Monday through Saturday, with no baiting; temporary stands and blinds must come out daily. Park hours are 8 a.m. to sunset with no hunting exception listed, and a 2021 DNR sheet says no hunting, so call 301-387-5563 before any hunt.
hunting.quote: The 122- acre designated hunting area is marked with managed hunting area signs. Hunting is permitted Monday-Saturday.

trapping.summary: Not without a written permit from the Superintendent of the Maryland Park Service, and we found no sign one is offered here. State park rules also bar removing or disturbing any animal, so ask the park at 301-387-5563.
trapping.quote: Except by written permit, an individual may not trap or attempt to trap game in a State park.

fishing.summary: On the Youghiogheny above Sang Run Bridge: lures only, no bait, no barbed hooks, release all trout. areas.note: Maryland's newest state park, formerly Savage River Lodge, is opening in phases and sits inside Savage River State Forest, so do not assume the forest's hunting and trapping rules apply on park land.

hunting.quote: Hunting opportunities and fishing in the Savage River are accessible nearby from the adjacent Savage River State Forest.

areas.manager: Maryland Park Service (Maryland Department of Natural Resources)
areas.contact: Swallow Falls State Park Office, 301-387-6938; Herrington Manor State Park Headquarters, 301-334-9180 (February and March)
areas.note: The park is open 8 a.m. to sunset, and day-use reservations are required on weekends and holidays from Memorial Day weekend through Labor Day.

areas.name: Islands of the Potomac Wildlife Management Area
areas.manager: Maryland DNR, Wildlife and Heritage Service
areas.contact: Western Region Main Office, 301-777-2136 (Allegany and Garrett). Gwynnbrook, 410-356-9272, is the office DNR names for the Montgomery islands.
areas.note: This area is 30 Potomac River islands reached only by water, and DNR's page names only three, all in Montgomery County, so call DNR's Western Region office (301-777-2136) to learn which islands in Allegany or Garrett County belong to it.

hunting.summary: DNR opens only Oxley, Mason and Maddox Islands to public hunting, all in Montgomery County, while state regulation lists this area for Allegany and doesn't bar hunting on it. Don't hunt an Allegany island until DNR's Western Region office (301-777-2136) confirms it is open.
hunting.quote: Of these Islands, three are open to public hunting in Montgomery County.

areas.name: Sideling Hill Wildlife Management Area
areas.manager: Maryland DNR, Wildlife and Heritage Service
areas.note: In its State Wildlands you may hunt, fish and trap only if otherwise permitted; motor vehicles, wheeled transport such as game carts, and temporary structures and equipment are barred. Ask about portable stands.
areas.waterNote: Sideling Hill Creek watershed is put-and-take trout water: release all brook trout immediately; other trout are limited to 5 a day and 10 in possession combined, with no minimum size. The 2026 Maryland fishing guide (https://www.eregulations.com/maryland/fishing/put-and-take-trout-fishing-areas) shows no closure.

hunting.summary: Hunting is allowed in open seasons with the usual licenses and stamps and no area permit, using temporary stands removed daily; Sunday hunting is limited and black bear requires a lottery-drawn permit. Neighboring Sideling Hill Creek State Park bans hunting, so follow boundary signs and ask the Indian Springs Wildlife Office, (301) 842-2702.
hunting.quote: No special permits or drawings are required to hunt this area, except appropriate licenses and stamps.

trapping.summary: Trapping requires a written use permit from DNR. Call the Indian Springs Wildlife Office at (301) 842-2702 for it.
trapping.quote: For trapping permit call (301) 842-2702

fishing.summary: Allowed with a Maryland nontidal fishing license, plus a trout stamp for trout if you're 16 or older. Green Ridge State Forest's page mentions stream closures on Sideling Hill Creek that the 2026 guide doesn't show, so ask DNR Fisheries, 301-334-8218, before a spring trip.
fishing.quote: Anglers will enjoy fishing for stocked trout in the shallow creek.

gathering.summary: State rules bar removing any portion of a plant or tree here without a use permit, but they don't name mushrooms or picked fruit and don't settle them. We found no sign a permit is offered for gathering, so ask the Indian Springs office at (301) 842-2702 before picking anything.

trapping.summary: Trapping here is by permit only. Call the Billmeyer Wildlife Office at (301) 478-2525 for a permit before you set anything.

areas.name: North Branch Potomac Fishery Management Area
areas.manager: Maryland DNR, Fishing and Boating Services
areas.contact: Maryland DNR Fishing and Boating Services, 1728 King's Run Road, Oakland, MD 21550, 301-334-8218
areas.note: Maryland's fishery regulation lists this area as North Branch Potomac River, Folly and Laurel Runs. The state's protected-lands map shows two Maryland-side tracts between those runs, but official boundaries are on DNR-held maps, so ask DNR for them before you go.
areas.waterNote: Under COMAR 08.02.11.01, the river from the red post below Blue Hole, about 1/3 mile upstream of Bench Mark 1110, down about 4 miles to Piney Swamp Run is artificial lures only, open all year: no natural or live bait or scented devices in possession, no barbed hooks, release all trout. Upstream to the post above Barnum, and from Piney Swamp Run down to the Allegany County line, is put-and-take trout water with no seasonal closure: no brook trout, 5 other trout a day, 10 in possession. COMAR 08.02.01.13 bars public access from the dam to the overhead cable and red bank post about 345 yards below the spillway, except with prior permission of facility staff or as posted. The Corps said in September 2025 that it opened the stilling basin behind the dam for fishing access, so follow the posted signs and ask DNR Fisheries at 301-334-8218 before fishing there.

hunting.summary: Maryland's fishery-area regulation lists this area as open to hunting, but the state hunting guide's public land list leaves it out. Ask DNR Fisheries at 301-334-8218 first; access runs only 5:30 a.m. to 10 p.m.
hunting.quote: Hunting is allowed in the following areas described in §C of this regulation

trapping.summary: Not without written permission from DNR's Fisheries Service, and we found no sign it is offered here. Ask DNR Fisheries at 301-334-8218.
trapping.quote: Trapping is only allowed in the areas described in §C of this regulation by written permission of the Fisheries Service.

fishing.summary: Open 5:30 a.m. to 10 p.m. with a state license, plus a trout stamp at 16 and older to catch, try to catch or keep trout; no bowfishing, gigs or spears. Most of the river appears lure-only, barbless, release-all-trout water, and public access is barred near the dam; confirm markers with DNR Fisheries at 301-334-8218.
fishing.quote: from a red post located below a pool known as Blue Hole approximately 1/3 mile upstream of Bench Mark 1110 on the Westernport U.S.G.S. Quadrangle, downstream approximately 4 miles to the confluence of Piney Swamp Run

ramps.summary: The rules for this fishery area have no plant-removal section and don't name ramps, and we found no other rule that settles digging here. That is not permission, so ask DNR Fisheries at 301-334-8218 first.

areas.manager: Maryland DNR, Fishing and Boating Services
areas.contact: DNR Freshwater Fisheries, Western Region I, Oakland: 301-334-8218

trapping.quote: Trapping is only allowed in the areas described in §C of this regulation by written permission of the Fisheries Service.

areas.manager: Maryland DNR, Fishing and Boating Services
areas.contact: Maryland DNR Fishing and Boating Services, 301-334-8218
areas.note: Also called Gary A. Yoder Landing or Black Oak, this is a public access site on the North Branch Potomac River near Rawlings, open 5:30 a.m. to 10 p.m.
areas.waterNote: DNR's river distances put this water in the North Branch catch-and-return area, which runs from Westernport down to the Route 956 bridge at Pinto (COMAR 08.02.11.01). There, no trout may be kept and no one may fish with a barbed hook.

DNR's river distances put this water in the North Branch catch-and-return area, so release trout and use barbless hooks for any species; questions go to DNR Fisheries at 301-334-8218.
fishing.quote: A person may not fish with any barbed hook.

gathering.summary: We found no rule for fishery management areas that covers picking mushrooms, berries or nuts, and that isn't permission. Ask DNR Fishing and Boating Services at 301-334-8218.

DNR's 2016 float-fishing article places McCoole four miles below Westernport, so ask DNR Fisheries at (301) 334-8218 if you need this confirmed.

hunting.summary: Open to hunting in season under normal Maryland rules; access runs 5:30 a.m. to 10 p.m., and Sunday hunting is limited. Stands and blinds must be temporary and removed daily; questions go to DNR Fisheries at (301) 334-8218.
hunting.quote: Hunting is allowed in the following areas described in §C of this regulation: (a) North Branch Potomac River — Laurel and Folly Run; and (b) North Branch Potomac River — McCoole.

trapping.summary: Not without written permission from DNR's Fisheries Service, and we found no sign it is offered here. Ask DNR Fisheries at (301) 334-8218.
trapping.quote: Trapping is only allowed in the areas described in §C of this regulation by written permission of the Fisheries Service.

fishing.summary: Open 5:30 a.m. to 10 p.m. with a Maryland nontidal license, plus a trout stamp for trout; projectile fishing gear is banned. DNR's river distances put this water in a catch-and-return stretch, so release every trout and use only barbless hooks, even for other species; ask DNR Fisheries at (301) 334-8218.
fishing.quote: A person may not fish with any barbed hook.

gathering.summary: We found no rule for this area that covers mushrooms, berries, nuts or other plants, and that is not permission. Ask DNR Fisheries at (301) 334-8218 before picking anything.

areas.name: Savage River Reservoir
areas.landType: Water supply and flood control reservoir
areas.manager: Upper Potomac River Commission
areas.contact: Upper Potomac River Commission, 528 Maryland Ave., Westernport, MD 21562, (301) 359-3944
areas.note: The Upper Potomac River Commission owns the reservoir, which is bordered by Savage River State Forest and, at its north end, Big Run State Park, so the rules on the shore can change from one owner to the next.
areas.waterNote: Reservoir (DNR fisheries page and Savage River State Forest recreation page): electric motors or paddle only, gas motors removed before launching, no gas cans in the boat; ice fishing is permitted. DNR's 2023 forest plan says shoreline access excludes the dam and spillway, so stay off them. Savage River from the reservoir up to Poplar Lick (COMAR 08.02.11.01): closed to all fishing from the first Sunday after March 4 to the last Saturday in March, except the youth trout day for anglers under 16. Savage River above Poplar Lick and the streams feeding the lake and river (COMAR 08.02.11.01 H(2)): artificial flies and lures only; the state fishing guide also bars barbed hooks there though the regulation doesn't, so use barbless. No bait or scented devices, and no brook trout kept. Questions: DNR Fisheries, 301-334-8218.

hunting.summary: We found no rule on hunting the Commission-owned reservoir or its shore, so don't take the state forest's hunting rule as covering it, and hunting is banned in Big Run State Park at the north end. Ask the Upper Potomac River Commission, (301) 359-3944.
hunting.quote: Hunting is permitted throughout Savage River State Forest except where posted with safety zone signs.

trapping.summary: Not without written permission, and we found no sign one is offered here; a state forest trapping permit isn't shown to cover this water. Ask the Upper Potomac River Commission, (301) 359-3944.
trapping.quote: Written permission is required to trap or hunt on another person’s property, including publicly owned properties.

fishing.summary: Open by boat or shore with a non-tidal license, plus a trout stamp at 16 and older to catch, try to catch or keep trout; release brook trout. DNR's park page reports a brief spring lake closure the state rule doesn't list, and the river above closes most of March; call DNR Fisheries, 301-334-8218, first.
fishing.quote: Fishing is permitted year-round with a non-tidal fishing license. Fishermen may find walleye, large mouth bass, crappie, yellow perch, bluegill, catfish, suckers, and trout. There is a brief lake closure each spring when trout stocking begins.

gathering.summary: We found no rule on picking mushrooms or berries on Commission land. The state forest around the reservoir bars removing plants, but that rule doesn't name mushrooms or berries, so ask the Upper Potomac River Commission, (301) 359-3944, or the forest office, 301-895-5759, first.
gathering.quote: an individual may not remove, disturb, damage, or destroy any plant, rock, mineral, or animal in a State forest.

ginseng.summary: Maryland Department of Agriculture's ginseng permit application bans harvest on land DNR manages, which includes the forest and park around the reservoir. The reservoir belongs to the Commission and we found no sign of its rule, so don't dig without asking the Commission, (301) 359-3944.
ginseng.quote: As of the 2013 collecting season, ginseng harvest on state lands managed by the Maryland Department of Natural Resources is no longer permitted.

ramps.summary: We found no plant rule for Commission land. The surrounding state forest bars removing plants, and we found no sign a permit is offered for ramps; that rule doesn't name ramps, so ask the Upper Potomac River Commission, (301) 359-3944, or the forest office, 301-895-5759, before digging.
ramps.quote: an individual may not remove, disturb, damage, or destroy any plant, rock, mineral, or animal in a State forest.

areas.name: Chesapeake and Ohio Canal National Historical Park
areas.manager: National Park Service
areas.note: Federal park rules apply here rather than state land rules, including on the canal towpath, which is also part of the Potomac Heritage National Scenic Trail.
areas.waterNote: Canal and basins: closed to swimming and wading. Cumberland: the lower side of the Inlet Lock is closed to the public. Potomac River: the six former Western Maryland Railroad bridges are closed. See the park's 2026 Superintendent's Compendium: https://www.nps.gov/choh/learn/management/upload/CHOH-Supt-Compendium-2026-508a.pdf

hunting.summary: No hunting in the park; you may only cross on foot during state seasons, at locations the park designates, to reach the Potomac or non-federal land. Keep guns unloaded, bows unstrung and dogs leashed, and call 301-739-4200 for crossing points before carrying a gun or bow across.
hunting.quote: The laws establishing C&O Canal do not authorize hunting.

trapping.summary: No trapping: National Park Service rules allow it only where a federal law calls for it, and we found no sign of such a law here. Questions go to the park at 301-739-4200.
trapping.quote: If there is no specific legal designation, then, by Federal regulation, hunting or trapping is not allowed in park units.

fishing.summary: Maryland license rules apply, but only attended hook and line, with no minnows, other bait fish, amphibians or unpreserved roe as bait, no chumming, no bait digging. Don't wade the canal or basins, fish from road bridges or public boat docks, or enter the Inlet Lock's lower side or Western Maryland Railroad bridges; call 301-739-4200.
fishing.quote: Possessing or using as bait for fishing in fresh waters, live or dead minnows or other bait fish, amphibians, nonpreserved fish eggs or fish roe, except in designated waters.

gathering.summary: By hand for personal use, with daily limits: 1 bushel of walnuts, hickory nuts, acorns or apples; 1/2 gallon of cherries, blackberries, raspberries, dewberries, strawberries, huckleberries, elderberries, paw paws or mushrooms; wineberries unlimited. Don't sell any or disturb the plant; anything unlisted is off limits; call 301-739-4200 about mushrooms, which federal rules don't name.
gathering.quote: Edible fruits, nuts, berries, and mushrooms may be gathered by hand for personal use or consumption. Commercial use is prohibited.

ginseng.summary: Not allowed: federal park rules ban digging or removing plants or their parts, and ginseng isn't on this park's gathering list, though the rule doesn't name ginseng. Questions go to the park at 301-739-4200.
ginseng.quote: Gathering or possessing undesignated natural products.

ramps.summary: Not allowed, even just a leaf: federal park rules ban digging or removing plants or their parts, and ramps aren't on this park's gathering list, though the rule doesn't name ramps. Questions go to the park at 301-739-4200.
ramps.quote: Gathering or possessing undesignated natural products.

areas.name: Jennings Randolph Lake
areas.manager: U.S. Army Corps of Engineers, Baltimore District
areas.note: The lake sits on the Maryland and West Virginia line, and the Corps lists the Maryland Boat Launch as run by others, so rules there may come from a different manager.
areas.waterNote: Lake: COMAR 08.02.11.01 B lists Jennings Randolph Lake as put-and-take trout water with no seasonal closure; release all brook trout; other trout 5 a day, 10 in possession. Stilling basin behind the dam: the Corps announced in September 2025 that it opened this for fishing access, but Maryland's rule bars public access from the dam to the overhead cable and red bank post about 345 yards below the spillway unless facility staff give prior permission or it is posted open. Follow the posted signs and ask the project office at (304) 355-2346 first. North Branch from about 345 yards below the spillway, downstream about 1 mile to a red post above Barnum, West Virginia: COMAR 08.02.11.01 C(3) allows artificial lures only, no barbed hooks, and all trout released. West Virginia banks: Maryland's fishing guide says a Maryland resident's Maryland nontidal license covers the West Virginia banks of the North Branch and the lake; West Virginia's license page says its other fishing rules apply and the agreement doesn't extend to tributaries.

hunting.summary: The Corps' 2025 map marks no-hunting areas around recreation sites, an archery-only area near the dam, and a section closed until November 25, then archery-only. It doesn't show firearms areas, so get the current map from the project office at (304) 355-2346 and ask whether it meets Maryland's written-permission rule and which state's license applies.
hunting.quote: Closed until November 25th - ArcheryOnly

trapping.summary: Not without written permission, and we found no sign one is offered here. Federal Corps rules allow trapping outside closed areas, but Maryland's guide requires written permission on publicly owned property, so ask the project office at (304) 355-2346 before setting a trap.
trapping.quote: Written permission is required to trap or hunt on another person’s property, including publicly owned properties.

fishing.summary: Below the dam, stay out of the first 345 yards unless posted open or staff approve; the next mile is lures only, release all trout. Fishing is allowed with a state license except in swimming areas, on boat ramps and other areas the Corps designates. In Maryland, trout take a stamp at 16 and older; release all brook trout on the Maryland side, and ask the project office at (304) 355-2346 about licenses across the state line.
fishing.quote: Fishing is permitted except in swimming areas, on boat ramps or other areas designated by the District Commander.

gathering.summary: Corps rules bar removing public property, including vegetative growth, and gathering parts of trees without written permission, but they don't name mushrooms, berries or nuts, so that doesn't settle picking them. Don't assume it's fine; ask the project office at (304) 355-2346 first.
gathering.quote: boundary monumentation or markers and vegetative growth, is prohibited except when in accordance with written permission of the District Commander.

ginseng.summary: Not without written permission from the Corps, and we found no sign one is offered here. Corps rules bar removing plants from project land, and a Maryland ginseng collecting permit doesn't replace that permission, so ask the project office at (304) 355-2346.
ginseng.quote: boundary monumentation or markers and vegetative growth, is prohibited except when in accordance with written permission of the District Commander.

ramps.summary: Not without written permission from the Corps, and we found no sign one is offered here. The Corps rule against removing vegetative growth doesn't name ramps, but it has no exception for them, so ask the project office at (304) 355-2346.
ramps.quote: boundary monumentation or markers and vegetative growth, is prohibited except when in accordance with written permission of the District Commander.

areas.name: Youghiogheny River Lake
areas.landType: Army Corps of Engineers lake project
areas.manager: U.S. Army Corps of Engineers, Pittsburgh District
areas.contact: Corps lake office, 497 Flanigan Road, Confluence, PA: (814) 395-3242. Maryland hunting guide number for Youghiogheny Reservoir Cooperative Wildlife Management Area: (301) 334-4255. Maryland DNR Fishing and Boating Services, Oakland: 301-334-8218.
areas.note: The lake crosses into Pennsylvania, and this covers the Maryland end in Garrett County, so get the boundary from the manager before you go.
areas.waterNote: Pennsylvania licenses: Maryland's fishing guide (https://www.eregulations.com/maryland/fishing/licenses-fees) lets a Pennsylvania resident with a Pennsylvania license fish the Maryland part of the reservoir, but not from shore or in tributaries, and defines the reservoir as running from the red posts on the Youghiogheny River down to the dam. DNR's lake page (https://dnr.maryland.gov/fisheries/pages/hotspots/youghiogheny.aspx) says boat anglers may fish the entire lake with either state's license and shoreline anglers need that state's license. Seasons and limits: the guide has a separate table for this lake (https://www.eregulations.com/maryland/fishing/youghiogheny-river-lake-seasons-sizes-limits); for example, walleye and sauger are open Jan. 1-March 14 and May 2-Dec. 31.

hunting.summary: Corps rules allow hunting unless closed, but we found no closure list for this lake and Maryland's guide says public property needs written permission, so ask the Corps at (814) 395-3242 first. Don't plan on Sundays, which the guide doesn't list for this land; Maryland's guide also lists a 900-acre cooperative wildlife area here that this page doesn't cover, so ask DNR at (301) 334-4255.
hunting.quote: Hunting is permitted except in areas and during periods where prohibited by the District Commander.

trapping.summary: Not without written permission, and we found no sign the Corps offers it; ask at (814) 395-3242. Maryland's guide also lists a 900-acre cooperative wildlife area here that this page doesn't cover, so ask DNR at (301) 334-4255.
trapping.quote: Written permission is required to trap or hunt on another person’s property, including publicly owned properties.

fishing.summary: Allowed with a Maryland license and this lake's own seasons and limits in Maryland's fishing guide, but not in swimming areas, on boat ramps or in areas the Corps closes. DNR's sources differ on when a Pennsylvania license counts here, so carry a Maryland license or call DNR Fisheries at 301-334-8218.
fishing.quote: Fishing is permitted except in swimming areas, on boat ramps or other areas designated by the District Commander.

gathering.summary: Corps rules bar removing vegetative growth without written permission, but that doesn't settle picked berries, nuts or mushrooms. Ask the Corps at (814) 395-3242 before you gather.
gathering.quote: vegetative growth, is prohibited except when in accordance with written permission of the District Commander.

ginseng.summary: Not without the Corps' written permission, and we found no sign it's offered here. Corps rules bar removing vegetative growth without it, so ask at (814) 395-3242.
ginseng.quote: vegetative growth, is prohibited except when in accordance with written permission of the District Commander.

ramps.summary: Not without the Corps' written permission, and we found no sign it's offered here. The rule against removing vegetative growth doesn't name ramps, so ask at (814) 395-3242.
ramps.quote: vegetative growth, is prohibited except when in accordance with written permission of the District Commander.

areas.name: Finzel Swamp Preserve
areas.manager: The Nature Conservancy
areas.note: Open to the public during daylight hours only, and dogs are not allowed.

hunting.summary: Not allowed unless posted at the preserve. TNC says several Maryland preserves have deer-hunting leases, but we found no sign Finzel is one, so ask TNC at (301) 897-8570.
hunting.quote: Fishing, trapping or hunting, except as otherwise posted

trapping.summary: Not allowed unless posted at the preserve, and we found no sign of a trapping exception at Finzel. Questions go to TNC at (301) 897-8570.
trapping.quote: Fishing, trapping or hunting, except as otherwise posted

fishing.summary: Not allowed unless posted at the preserve, and a Maryland fishing license does not change that. We found no sign of a fishing exception at Finzel; ask TNC at (301) 897-8570.
fishing.quote: Fishing, trapping or hunting, except as otherwise posted

gathering.summary: TNC bans picking mushrooms and flowers at its Maryland preserves. Berries and nuts are not named, but the same rules bar removing any part of the landscape, so leave them too; ask TNC at (301) 897-8570.
gathering.quote: Picking flowers, mushrooms, etc.

ginseng.summary: TNC's rules bar removing any part of the landscape. They don't name ginseng, but digging it falls under that ban and we found no collecting permit offered here; ask TNC at (301) 897-8570.
ginseng.quote: Removing rocks or other parts of the landscape

ramps.summary: TNC's rules bar removing any part of the landscape. They don't name ramps, but digging or picking them falls under that ban and we found no collecting permit offered here; ask TNC at (301) 897-8570.
ramps.quote: Removing rocks or other parts of the landscape

areas.name: Cranesville Swamp Preserve
areas.manager: The Nature Conservancy
areas.contact: TNC in Maryland/DC: (301) 897-8570, contactMDDC@tnc.org. TNC in West Virginia: (304) 637-0160, westvirginia@tnc.org.
areas.note: Private land owned by The Nature Conservancy, open year-round in daylight, with no dogs allowed. These are TNC's Maryland/DC rules, so on the Preston County, West Virginia side ask TNC West Virginia at (304) 637-0160.

hunting.summary: TNC's rules ban hunting unless posted at the preserve, and we found no sign a permit is offered here. An older Cranesville guide mentions a permitted deer hunt and current rules mention deer leases at unnamed preserves, so ask TNC at (301) 897-8570.
hunting.quote: Fishing, trapping or hunting, except as otherwise posted

trapping.summary: TNC's preserve rules ban trapping unless a sign at the preserve says otherwise. We found no exception listed online, so ask TNC at (301) 897-8570 before relying on one.
trapping.quote: Fishing, trapping or hunting, except as otherwise posted

fishing.summary: TNC's preserve rules ban fishing unless a sign at the preserve says otherwise. We found no exception listed online, so ask TNC at (301) 897-8570 before relying on one.
fishing.quote: Fishing, trapping or hunting, except as otherwise posted

gathering.summary: TNC's rules ban picking mushrooms by name, along with flowers and the like. They don't name berries and a 2014 TNC guide said visitors could pick blueberries, but the 2023 rules are newer and stricter, so ask TNC at (301) 897-8570 before picking any.
gathering.quote: Picking flowers, mushrooms, etc.

ginseng.summary: TNC's rules ban removing parts of the landscape and picking flowers and the like. They don't name ginseng, but don't dig it here; questions go to TNC at (301) 897-8570.
ginseng.quote: Removing rocks or other parts of the landscape

ramps.summary: TNC's rules ban removing parts of the landscape and picking flowers and the like. They don't name ramps, but don't dig or cut them here; questions go to TNC at (301) 897-8570.
ramps.quote: Removing rocks or other parts of the landscape

areas.name: Sideling Hill Creek Preserve
areas.manager: The Nature Conservancy
areas.note: This Nature Conservancy preserve is open during daylight hours, and dogs aren't allowed. Its Bryant Tract trailhead is in Washington County and its Yonker Tract in Allegany; the rules of Sideling Hill Creek State Park and Sideling Hill Wildlife Management Area don't apply here.

hunting.summary: Not allowed unless signs at the preserve say otherwise. The Nature Conservancy says several Maryland preserves have deer-hunting leases but doesn't say this is one, so call (301) 897-8570 before planning a hunt.
hunting.quote: Fishing, trapping or hunting, except as otherwise posted

trapping.summary: Not allowed unless signs at the preserve say otherwise, and we found no sign of a trapping exception here. Questions go to The Nature Conservancy at (301) 897-8570.
trapping.quote: Fishing, trapping or hunting, except as otherwise posted

fishing.summary: Not allowed on the preserve unless signs say otherwise, and we found no sign of a fishing exception here. Before fishing the creek where it runs through or beside the preserve, ask The Nature Conservancy at (301) 897-8570.
fishing.quote: Fishing, trapping or hunting, except as otherwise posted

gathering.summary: Picking mushrooms is banned by name. Berries and nuts aren't named but appear to fall under the same rule's "etc.", so treat them as off limits unless The Nature Conservancy at (301) 897-8570 tells you otherwise.
gathering.quote: Picking flowers, mushrooms, etc.

ginseng.summary: The preserve's rules don't name ginseng, but they ban removing parts of the landscape, which covers digging it. We found no sign of any permission here; ask The Nature Conservancy at (301) 897-8570.
ginseng.quote: Removing rocks or other parts of the landscape

ramps.summary: The preserve's rules don't name ramps, but they ban removing parts of the landscape, which covers digging them. We found no sign of any permission here; ask The Nature Conservancy at (301) 897-8570.
ramps.quote: Removing rocks or other parts of the landscape

areas.name: Selinger Marsh
areas.manager: The Nature Conservancy
areas.note: Open year round, dawn to dusk, with no facilities, trails or established parking, and dogs are not allowed. During hunting season The Nature Conservancy asks visitors to its preserves to wear blaze orange and avoid early morning and evening.

hunting.summary: The Nature Conservancy's preserve rules ban hunting unless signs say otherwise, and we found no public hunting offered here. Call the Conservancy at (301) 897-8570 with questions.
hunting.quote: Fishing, trapping or hunting, except as otherwise posted

trapping.summary: The Nature Conservancy's preserve rules ban trapping unless signs say otherwise, and we found no exception for this preserve. Call the Conservancy at (301) 897-8570 with questions.
trapping.quote: Fishing, trapping or hunting, except as otherwise posted

fishing.summary: The Nature Conservancy's preserve rules ban fishing unless signs say otherwise, and we found no exception for this preserve. Call the Conservancy at (301) 897-8570 with questions.
fishing.quote: Fishing, trapping or hunting, except as otherwise posted

gathering.summary: The Nature Conservancy's preserve rules ban picking flowers, mushrooms and the like. Berries and nuts aren't named, so treat them as off limits unless the Conservancy tells you otherwise at (301) 897-8570.
gathering.quote: Picking flowers, mushrooms, etc.

ginseng.summary: The Nature Conservancy's preserve rules ban removing parts of the landscape. They don't name ginseng, but treat digging it here as banned unless the Conservancy tells you otherwise at (301) 897-8570.
ginseng.quote: Removing rocks or other parts of the landscape

ramps.summary: The Nature Conservancy's preserve rules ban picking flowers, mushrooms and the like and removing parts of the landscape. They don't name ramps, but treat digging bulbs or taking leaves here as banned unless the Conservancy tells you otherwise at (301) 897-8570.
ramps.quote: Removing rocks or other parts of the landscape

areas.name: Potomac Highlands Preserve
areas.manager: The Nature Conservancy
areas.note: The Nature Conservancy's page says open to the public but puts recreation and permitted hunting after a future access plan. We found no sign a plan has been adopted and there are no maintained trails or facilities, so ask (301) 897-8570 before you go.

hunting.summary: Not open to public hunting: The Nature Conservancy's Maryland preserve rules ban it unless posted, and its 2025 report says permitted hunting is only something a future access plan may include. Ask about leases or postings at (301) 897-8570.
hunting.quote: Fishing, trapping or hunting, except as otherwise posted

trapping.summary: The Nature Conservancy's Maryland preserve rules ban trapping unless posted, and we found no sign it is offered here. Ask the Conservancy at (301) 897-8570.
trapping.quote: Fishing, trapping or hunting, except as otherwise posted

fishing.summary: The Nature Conservancy's Maryland preserve rules ban fishing from preserve land unless posted. The Conservancy describes this land as adjacent to the North Branch and bordering the Jennings Randolph Lake recreation area, so a bank here may be preserve land; ask at (301) 897-8570 before fishing from it or crossing it.
fishing.quote: Fishing, trapping or hunting, except as otherwise posted

gathering.summary: The Nature Conservancy's Maryland preserve rules ban picking mushrooms by name. Berries and nuts aren't named but fall under the rule's "etc.", so treat them as off limits unless the Conservancy says otherwise at (301) 897-8570.
gathering.quote: Picking flowers, mushrooms, etc.

ginseng.summary: The Nature Conservancy's Maryland preserve rules ban removing parts of the landscape. They don't name ginseng, but digging it removes part of the land, so don't dig here; questions go to (301) 897-8570.
ginseng.quote: Removing rocks or other parts of the landscape

ramps.summary: The Nature Conservancy's Maryland preserve rules ban removing parts of the landscape and picking plants such as flowers. The rules don't name ramps, but digging or cutting them falls under those bans; questions go to (301) 897-8570.
ramps.quote: Removing rocks or other parts of the landscape

areas.name: Carey Run Sanctuary
areas.manager: Maryland Ornithological Society
areas.note: The grounds are free and open to the public for nature study and hiking, but the farmhouse is for Maryland Ornithological Society members or approved project groups by reservation and is closed from late October through early April.

hunting.summary: No hunting and no weapons at this sanctuary. Deer stands on neighboring land don't mean hunting is allowed here; ask the Sanctuary Chair (sanctuary@mdbirds.org) with questions.
hunting.quote: Hunting is not allowed at the sanctuary, but there are active deer stands on neighboring land and perhaps on-site poaching.

trapping.summary: No trapping. The narrow exceptions, such as a management program approved in advance by the Maryland Ornithological Society's board, aren't open to ordinary visitors; ask the Sanctuary Chair (sanctuary@mdbirds.org) with questions.
trapping.quote: Hunting and trapping are prohibited, with the exception of specific management programs approved in advance by the MOS Board of Directors.

fishing.summary: The public rules don't name fishing and ban removing any animals, while the rules for personal visits, written for members' overnight stays, say recreational fishing is permitted. Ask the Sanctuary Chair (sanctuary@mdbirds.org) before you fish, and don't keep fish without a clear answer.
fishing.quote: No removal of any animals or plants

gathering.summary: The rules ban removing any plants, but they don't name mushrooms or berries, so that isn't settled. Don't gather here unless the Sanctuary Chair (sanctuary@mdbirds.org) says you can.
gathering.quote: No removal of any animals or plants

ginseng.summary: The rules don't name ginseng, but they ban removing any plants, and we found no sign of any permission for harvest. Ask the Sanctuary Chair (sanctuary@mdbirds.org).
ginseng.quote: No removal of any animals or plants

ramps.summary: The rules don't name ramps, but they ban removing any plants, and we found no sign of any permission for harvest. Ask the Sanctuary Chair (sanctuary@mdbirds.org).
ramps.quote: No removal of any animals or plants

areas.name: Chandler & Eleanor Robbins Sanctuary at Red Run
areas.manager: Maryland Ornithological Society
areas.note: Open during daylight hours for nature study, with weapons banned; private land surrounds this 45-acre sanctuary, so park at the Guthrie Lane spot and stay within its boundaries.

hunting.summary: No hunting on the sanctuary, and weapons are banned. Hunting happens on the private land next door, so wear blaze orange in season; questions go to the Maryland Ornithological Society at sanctuary@mdbirds.org.
hunting.quote: Hunting is not permitted on sanctuary grounds, but takes place on neighboring private lands.

trapping.summary: The sanctuary rules ban trapping by name. Questions go to the Maryland Ornithological Society at sanctuary@mdbirds.org.
trapping.quote: No hunting or trapping

fishing.summary: The rules don't name fishing, but they ban removing any animals, so you can't keep a fish. Catch-and-release isn't settled, so ask the Maryland Ornithological Society at sanctuary@mdbirds.org before fishing Red Run here.
fishing.quote: No removal of any animals or plants

gathering.summary: The sanctuary bans removing plants, but that rule doesn't name mushrooms, berries or nuts and doesn't by itself settle fungi or picked fruit. Don't gather here unless the Maryland Ornithological Society says you can: sanctuary@mdbirds.org.
gathering.quote: No removal of any animals or plants

ginseng.summary: Don't dig ginseng here: the sanctuary bans removing any plants, and a state ginseng season doesn't override that rule on this private land. Questions go to the Maryland Ornithological Society at sanctuary@mdbirds.org.
ginseng.quote: No removal of any animals or plants

ramps.summary: Don't dig ramps or take their leaves here: the sanctuary's ban on removing any plants doesn't name ramps, but it covers all plants. Questions go to the Maryland Ornithological Society at sanctuary@mdbirds.org.
ramps.quote: No removal of any animals or plants

areas.name: Caroline W. Wilson Sanctuary
areas.manager: Maryland Ornithological Society
areas.note: Open for nature study in daylight, but landlocked: the MOS guide's only route is on foot along active CSX tracks, with no sign the railroad permits that. Ask the MOS Sanctuary Chair (sanctuary@mdbirds.org) before you go; neighboring Deer Park Spring Water land is closed.

hunting.summary: The MOS guide bans hunting and weapons here, though MOS says hunting is allowed at certain unlisted sites and the guide mentions local deer hunters, so ask the MOS Sanctuary Chair (sanctuary@mdbirds.org). Neighboring land is hunted, so wear blaze orange in season.
hunting.quote: Hunting is not permitted on sanctuary grounds, but may take place on neighboring lands.

trapping.summary: No trapping on the sanctuary. Questions go to the MOS Sanctuary Chair (sanctuary@mdbirds.org).
trapping.quote: No hunting or trapping

fishing.summary: The rules don't name fishing, but they ban removing any animals, so don't keep fish. Ask the MOS Sanctuary Chair (sanctuary@mdbirds.org) before fishing the Little Youghiogheny here, even catch-and-release.
fishing.quote: No removal of any animals or plants

gathering.summary: The rules ban removing plants and MOS applies Leave No Trace at its sanctuaries, but neither names mushrooms or picked fruit, so they don't settle it. Don't gather here unless the MOS Sanctuary Chair (sanctuary@mdbirds.org) says you can.
gathering.quote: No removal of any animals or plants

ginseng.summary: Don't dig ginseng here: the sanctuary's rules ban removing any plants and give no exception, though they don't name ginseng. Questions go to the MOS Sanctuary Chair (sanctuary@mdbirds.org).
ginseng.quote: No removal of any animals or plants

ramps.summary: Don't dig ramps or cut their leaves here: the sanctuary's rules ban removing any plants and give no exception, though they don't name ramps. Questions go to the MOS Sanctuary Chair (sanctuary@mdbirds.org).
ramps.quote: No removal of any animals or plants

areas.name: Great Allegheny Passage in Allegany County
areas.manager: Allegany County Government
areas.contact: Allegany County Government 301-777-2526, 701 Kelly Road, Cumberland, MD 21502
areas.note: The county's rules cover the 22-mile trail right-of-way from Cumberland to the Pennsylvania line, open dawn to dusk only; using the trail gives you no right to hunt, fish or gather on the land beside it.

hunting.summary: No hunting on the trail right-of-way, and no loaded firearms or other loaded harvest devices on it. It is open for hunting access only during Maryland's regulated season or with written county authorization, dawn to dusk, and driving on it needs county authorization; ask Allegany County, 301-777-2526.
hunting.quote: Hunting is prohibited in the ROW. The transport of loaded firearms or any loaded device designed to harvest game animals is prohibited in the ROW.

trapping.summary: Not without written permission, and we found no sign one is offered here. Ask Allegany County, 301-777-2526.
trapping.quote: Written permission is required to trap or hunt on another person’s property, including publicly owned properties.

fishing.summary: The county's trail rules don't mention fishing; Maryland DNR's trail page says anglers use the trail to reach fishing spots, but that isn't a rule allowing it. Stay out of the railroad track area between Cumberland and Frostburg except at designated crossings, and ask the county first: 301-777-2526.
fishing.quote: Fishermen take the trail to favorite fishing spots.

gathering.summary: The county's trail rules don't mention mushrooms, berries, nuts or plants, and that isn't permission. Ask the county before picking anything: 301-777-2526.

ginseng.summary: The county's trail rules don't name ginseng or digging, though they bar altering the trail without written county authorization, and we found no sign the trail is listed as state DNR land. Don't dig here unless the county approves it: 301-777-2526.

ramps.summary: The county's trail rules don't name ramps and have no general plant-removal rule, though they bar altering the trail without written county authorization. Don't dig here unless the county approves it: 301-777-2526.

areas.name: Piney Reservoir
areas.manager: City of Frostburg owns the shoreline and its Public Works handles hunting permission; Maryland DNR Fisheries manages the fishery
areas.contact: City of Frostburg Public Works, 37 S Broadway, Frostburg: 301-689-6000, ext. 111. Fishing questions: Maryland DNR Fishing and Boating Services, Oakland: 301-334-8218.
areas.note: This is the City of Frostburg's water supply on city-owned shoreline, and the only public access DNR describes is shoreline and ice fishing, with no boats.

hunting.summary: City land: you need the city's written permission, by filling out a form with your hunting license information at Public Works, City Hall, 37 S Broadway, Frostburg. That process comes from a 2023 city reply, so call 301-689-6000, ext. 111 first to confirm.
hunting.quote: To get written hunting permission for Piney, you must come into City Hall, located at 37 S Broadway, and fill out a form that requires your hunting license information.

trapping.summary: Not without written permission, and we found no sign the city offers it for trapping. Ask Frostburg Public Works at 301-689-6000, ext. 111.
trapping.quote: Written permission is required to trap or hunt on another person’s property, including publicly owned properties.

fishing.summary: Shoreline and ice fishing only, with a Maryland license, plus a trout stamp at 16 and older to catch, try to catch or keep trout; release all brook trout. No boats, the posted dam face is closed to fishing, and questions go to DNR Fisheries at 301-334-8218.
fishing.quote: public access for shoreline and ice fishing is permitted. No fishing is permitted along the face of the dam and is posted accordingly. Boating is not permitted on Piney Reservoir.

gathering.summary: This is city water supply land, the city's own rules on gathering here are unsettled, and the public access DNR describes is for fishing. Ask Frostburg Public Works at 301-689-6000, ext. 111 before gathering.
gathering.quote: The entire shoreline of Piney Reservoir is owned by the City of Frostburg and public access for shoreline and ice fishing is permitted.

ginseng.summary: This is city land, so Maryland's ban on DNR-managed land does not settle it, and the city's own rules on digging here are unsettled. Ask Frostburg Public Works at 301-689-6000, ext. 111 before digging.
ginseng.quote: The entire shoreline of Piney Reservoir is owned by the City of Frostburg and public access for shoreline and ice fishing is permitted.

ramps.summary: The city's own rules on digging plants here are unsettled, and no Maryland rule we found names ramps. Ask Frostburg Public Works at 301-689-6000, ext. 111 before digging.
ramps.quote: The entire shoreline of Piney Reservoir is owned by the City of Frostburg and public access for shoreline and ice fishing is permitted.
